Hi *[NAME],*

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *[DATE].*

Drivers are considered independent contractors providing transportation services via Bolt platform. Due to this, Bolt only stores invoices, pay statement and balance reports of the drivers. 

We must point out that this information can be accessed via your Driver Portal available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/login?isPasswordReset=true&shortlink=lvew0z3s&c=Global|https://partners.bolt.eu/login?isPasswordReset=true&shortlink=lvew0z3s&c=Global|smart-link] . You can find this information by navigating to the following areas of the portal:

* Invoices issued to riders from you as a driver available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/rider-invoices|https://partners.bolt.eu/rider-invoices|smart-link] 
* Invoices issued to you as a driver by Bolt [https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices|https://partners.bolt.eu/invoices|smart-link] 
* Pay statements can be accessed via Payouts available at[ |https://partners.bolt.eu/payouts][https://partners.bolt.eu/payout|https://partners.bolt.eu/payout|smart-link] 
* Balance reports available at[https://partners.bolt.eu/balance-reports|https://partners.bolt.eu/balance-reports|smart-link] 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Sincerely,
Bolt

Hi [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] 

Thanks for the updated summary. My thoughts:

*(1) Sending the email to drivers asking them to take part in the competition*

I agree that the lawful basis should be {color:#4c9aff}*legitimate interest*{color} in promoting our services and conducting sweepstakes to deepen our existing relationship with our drivers / develop new ones). 

Important note - while the changes are already added to the pending 2024 Driver PN, the current live Driver PN is silent on direct marketing activities altogether. This is a known gap and it is pending resolution with the future Driver PN update.

The last update I had from Gab - we're estimating to have the Driver PN final draft ready by end of August. So, we should keep in mind that there is a gap in our transparency compliance for drivers.

On a positive note, we do include the following disclaimer on the [website|https://bolt.eu/en/driver/], which de-risks the gap to an extent:

_“Once you’ve become a driver, we will occasionally send you offers and promotions related to our services. You can always unsubscribe by changing your communication preferences.”_

----

*(2) Collecting the driver’s name and email in the form*

I agree that this is low risk, not excessive, and for a relatively clear purpose. As this personal data is required to participate in the campaign, I would advise to rely on GDPR Art. 6.1(b) as the lawful basis instead of consent. I believe, for similar cases legal have used the [Campaign T&C|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ybRlet8ae-IPsv5T7MemwjSEYiNGi0afYS5DQS3Nzb8/edit?usp=sharing], which includes Section 6 on privacy [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] .

Consent must be free - and in this case, it's required to participate in the Campaign. If the driver does not agree to the processing, they cannot participate - so not sure consent would be “freely given”.

In the Collection Form itself, we could add that the activity is governed by the Campaign T&C, and for information on how Bolt processes your personal data, please refer to Section 6 of the T&C.

----

*(3) Processing the driver’s data about completed trips / driver rating / number of friends invited to the platform*

I agree with your concerns re/ *(2) information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS* .

---
- name: Fix IAM profile and Rename AWS credentials file
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Change IAM Profile
      amazon.aws.ec2_instance:
        region: "{{ aws_region }}"
        instance_ids:
          - "{{ hostvars[inventory_hostname]['instance_id'] }}"
        iam_instance_profile: "mysql.backup"
      register: ec2_result
      delegate_to: localhost
      become: false

     - name: Display results
      debug:
        var: ec2_result
        
    - name: Check if the AWS credentials file exists
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /root/.aws/credentials
      register: credentials_file

    - name: Copy the AWS credentials file to the new name
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /root/.aws/credentials
        dest: /root/.aws/credentials_not_in_use
        mode: 0600
        remote_src: yes
      when: credentials_file.stat.exists

    - name: Remove the original AWS credentials file
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /root/.aws/credentials
        state: absent
      when: credentials_file.stat.exists

    - name: Check if the AWS credentials_not_in_use file exists
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /root/.aws/credentials_not_in_use
      register: credentials_not_in_use_file
    
    - name: Set Permissions
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /root/.aws/credentials_not_in_use
        state: file
        mode: '0600'
      when: credentials_not_in_use_file.stat.exists

Once rollback is in progress, we should show the health check status in the heart icon (the same way as we do for the average deployments (see attached screenshot). The reason is that a “successful deployment” in the Kubernetes world means that the deployment manifest was successfully applied. Once the manifest is applied, Kubernetes tries to get to the desired state. Checking if the desired state is met or not is the responsibility of the health check. 

For rollbacks, we don’t show the health check status in the “heart” icon, which might be wrongly interpreted by a user as a fully successful rollback. So, the proposed solution is to:

# Make health check status visible in the “heart” icon for the rollbacks - this logic is on the UI [https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/master/builder/packages/frontend/admin/modules/builder-ui/src/components/pipeline-step-templates/ReleaseReadyUserValidationTemplate.tsx|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/master/builder/packages/frontend/admin/modules/builder-ui/src/components/pipeline-step-templates/ReleaseReadyUserValidationTemplate.tsx] 
# Make sure that if the rollback deployment fails not even reaching the health check status, we show 1/1 and not 0/1 (it should be the default case, just need to double check that it works like this). Logic is on UI as well.

PL: Hi All, we maintain our position that we should support safety of riders, however, Bolt should not be directly involved in providing dashcams to the drivers as this could be considered as providing work equipment. Bolt can negotiate a deal with the dashcams provider but it is the fleet that should be purchasing them.

Please also note that privacy issues are strictly verified and analysed by Polish authorities (e.g. Bolt is expecting a decision re. direct marrketing that - if unfavourable - may result in fine imposed on Bolt in the amount of up to max of 4% of Bolt annual global turnover), therefore our solutions has to be approved by the privacy team.

Currently we have all logs for relayed emails in the ses-forwarders. Unfortunately this might not be a straightforward when sending logs through SES. All of the ways to monitor sending activity are described in the table here: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/monitor-sending-activity.html|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/monitor-sending-activity.html|smart-link]

If we want to mimic the current level of detail, then we are interested in logging details for each event. This boils it down to these options:

!image-20240808-085724.png|width=1245,height=374,alt="image-20240808-085724.png"!

Currently, in ses-forwarders, we are logging all relays. The most 1:1 interpretation of this would be logging all sends in SES. That narrows our options down to the middle row on the table depicted above - event publishing. It mentions CloudWatch, which would lead you to believe that one can send the events into a CloudWatch log group, however that is not the case. Instead it only sends them there as metrics, which is not what we need.

One solution to have all sends logged would be using SNS + Lambda to store the send events as logs in CloudWatch. The other one might be Firehose, however that doesn’t seem to be something we are currently using and familiar with.

It’s also worth mentioning that CloudWatch logs ingestion is not exactly cheap either.

I will consult with Comms about their need for logs and also keep investigating our opportunities for that.

Lighthouse Advice:
{panel}

+*Question 1 – Are there explicit legal obligations under the Tax Administration Act (Quebec) to share data with Revenu Québec?*+

Yes. As set out in more detail below, there are clear legal requirements under the [+Tax Administration Act (Quebec)+|https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/a-6.002] for sharing data with Revenu Québec:

* *Section 37.1.5 of the Tax Administration Act* states that anyone required to be registered under [+Division II of Chapter VIII.1 of Title I of the Act+|https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1?&target=] respecting the Québec sales tax must electronically file both their registration application and return, following the Minister’s specified terms and conditions.
* *Section 350.62 of Division II of Chapter VIII.1 of Title I of the Act respecting the Québec sales tax* requires anyone engaged in a “taxi business” to send the prescribed information to the Minister in the prescribed manner and timeframe. Additionally, they must provide an invoice with the required information to the passenger at the end of the trip and retain a copy.

* Definition of “taxi business”: According to the Act respecting the Québec sales tax, a “taxi business” includes:

* A business of transporting passengers by taxi or similar vehicle for regulated fares.
* A business of transporting passengers for a fare by motor vehicle, organised or coordinated through an electronic platform, excluding certain types of transportation like sightseeing services or school transportation.

Bolt falls under the second definition of a “taxi business,” as it coordinates passenger transportation via an electronic platform, the Bolt App. This classification means that Bolt is subject to the information sharing obligations under the Tax Administration Act and the Act respecting the Québec sales tax.

* *Prescribed information*: Details of the prescribed information to be sent to Revenu Quebec are provided on Revenu Quebec’s [+website+|https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/sector-specific-measures/mandatory-billing/mandatory-billing-sending-information/], including:

* detailed fare data, 
* invoice details - Bolt must provide an invoice to the passenger that includes necessary details such as the date, time, duration, and cost of the trip. A copy of this invoice must also be retained by Bolt.
* Vehicles must be equipped with a certified SRS system for the purpose of tracking and sending prescribed information to Revenu Quebec. Each driver must be set up as a user on the SRS system, so it is possible that driver personal data will be included in the information that is provided to Revenu Quebec via the SRS system. 

+*Question 2 – Does the*+ [+*Act respecting Access to documents held by public bodies and the Protection of personal information (Québec)*+|https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/A-2.1/19991022#:~:text=Every%20person%20has%20a%20right,30%2C%20s.] +*(“Act”) require Revenu Québec to protect the data it receives and process it according to specific data protection standards?*+

Yes, the Act outlines specific responsibilities for Revenu Québec to safeguard the confidentiality and integrity of the data it handles. Below, we set out the key features of the Act which require Revenu Québec to protect the data it receives:

* *Confidentiality Obligations (Sections 53-56)*: The Act classifies nominative information (data identifying an individual) as confidential. Disclosure is tightly controlled and allowed only under certain conditions, such as with the individual’s consent or for legal proceedings.
* *Conditions for Disclosure (Sections 59-60)*: Revenu Québec may release nominative information without consent in limited, strictly regulated scenarios, such as for legal actions or crime prevention efforts. They must confirm the necessity of releasing such information for the stated purposes before proceeding.
* *Data Management Standards (Sections 64-65)*: The collection of nominative information must be essential for the public body’s operations. Individuals must be informed about the data collection purpose, who will access the data, and how it will be used.
* *Rights to Access and Correction (Sections 83-93)*: The Act provides persons concerned (i.e., the data subject) rights to access and correct personal information. Revenu Québec is required to facilitate these rights, allowing individuals to review and amend their data when necessary.
* *Regulatory Compliance (Section 76)*: Public bodies like Revenu Québec must document their data processing activities and report them to the Commission d’accès à l’information, ensuring their practices are transparent and accountable.

Revenu Québec is mandated to process personal data with a high degree of care, reflecting broader data protection principles of confidentiality and transparency in data processing.

+*Additional Consideration – Assessing the Need for a Data Sharing Agreement in the Context of Potential Restricted Transfers under the GDPR*+*:*

As Bolt Operations OÜ is based within the EU and stores personal data there, sharing personal data with Revenu Quebec to comply with the information-sharing requirements under the Tax Administration Act (Québec) _may_ involve transferring personal data from the EU to a non-EU country, Canada. However, if the collection and sharing of the prescribed data are managed locally by the SRS system installed in each vehicle in Quebec, this could potentially eliminate the need for data transfers from the EU to Canada. 

If, however, there will still be instances where personal data must be transmitted from Bolt’s EU operations to Revenu Québec, then appropriate safeguards would need to be put in place to legitimise the potential restricted transfer to Canada. This is necessary because the European Commission’s adequacy decision, which recognises Canada’s alignment with EU data protection standards, applies only to commercial, private-sector entities regulated by Canada’s Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (“*PIPEDA*”). Revenu Québec, however, is governed by Quebec’s provincial privacy laws, such as the Act respecting Access to documents held by public bodies and the Protection of personal information (Québec) and is not covered under PIPEDA. Consequently, the adequacy decision does not extend to data transfers to Revenu Québec.

Given this gap, Bolt may need to implement appropriate safeguards for these transfers, including the use of SCCs. In the absence of a data sharing agreement, SCCs must be executed independently. Furthermore, if a data transfer impact assessment indicates the necessity for additional safeguards, a data sharing agreement may be required to formalise these safeguards contractually.

Hej, similar to the tax advise shared a while ago for CZ and HR, see below for RO and SK, with some specificities:

* Similar to CZ and HR markets, both RO and SK markets are Centralised when it comes to Bolt Food. I would expect that initial marketing costs (stickers, etc) would be borne by Bolt Local Entities in those countries, while the cost and the invoicing of the branding/incentive bonus will take place at the level of Bolt Ops OU, since it is the entity holding the contractual relationship with Delivery partners.

* Reclass risk: Given the % composition of the RO and SK markets in terms of Couriers and Fleets, I do believe it would make more sense to engage with Fleets (i.e. less risky).

* I understand that the incentive bonus should be invoiced separately from other items and fees (i.e. through a separate line item within the invoice to Fleets), in CZ, SK and HR. Do we already know how this incentive will be named/shown in the invoice? We should avoid any reference to "additional delivery cost". 

*NB!* Due to a current tax issue we are experiencing in RO involving fleets and RO Tax authorities, we are working on merging all other fees (example: Waiting time compensation fee, Delivery Bonus fee, etc.) due from Bolt Ops OU to Fleets under “Marketplace Fees”, in the invoices. Thus, it would be interesting to include as well this Branding bonus within it, at least in the invocies (of course, later on the fleets will be able to see a detailed breakdown of the earned fees in their specific weekly reports). 

* We need to stress to the fleets in RO and SK that they need to register for European VAT number (VIES, which is like an upgrade of the local VAT number) in order to perform this cross-border service (Fleets in RO or SK, to Bolt Ops OU in EE).

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 July 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

*Your rights*

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Supplier Ags Worldwide Movers Limited has sent us an invoice:

|NSSF APPLICATION FEE|26638.44|16%|

For my calculations, our extended amount should then be 53276.88 and tax 8524.3008. Giving total amount of 53276.88 + 8524.3008 = this is giving 61801.1808. 

Supplier has stated on the invoice (excluding VAT) that they expect 45928.34 KES, and VAT of 300 USD (as of today, conversion shows 38,850.00)

The invoice booked in Telema shows me the following:

# Coding Lines for 45,928.34 KES & 16% TAX rate. 
# Rounding line for 0.01 and 0% tax rate.

In Telema, they populate the values for:

Without VAT: 45,928.34
VAT: 7348.53
Total (KES): 53,276.88

In Workday, we see two lines:

# 45,928.34 with 16% and 5% tax rate, this seems some local tax process? 🙂 
# Rounding line for 0.05.

If I also take you to the tax tab: 

!image-20240808-181133.png|width=2913,height=1111,alt="image-20240808-181133.png"!

!image-20240808-181053.png|width=2469,height=1391,alt="image-20240808-181053.png"!

Workday recognises one line has 16% tax rate, and this is the tax due: 

45,928.34*0.16 = 7,348.53 (match up with Telema).

!image-20240808-181357.png|width=3450,height=1200,alt="image-20240808-181357.png"!

By looking at audit trail, I can see that on 04/01, Siret had made a manual change to the invoice to “fix the amounts”. 

______

I will make a comment, about why this is happening, and “fix” for this in next comment. 🙂

The Finance Technology team, is already aware of the rounding issue, and I share the links below to “tackling” this issue, in a two-fold manner.

The problem statement here, is that our integration only takes whatever data is in Telema. Telema does their own algorithm, to aggregate lines then add a rounding line for it. This means that Workday, when it processes the invoice it sees a “lesser” amount, to apply the 16% tax rate for.

Integrations by design principles should never manipulate data, especially financial ones. 

[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WDFT-2243|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WDFT-2243|smart-link] 
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WDFT-2299|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WDFT-2299|smart-link]  

We have already in-flight *Total Control Amount* improvement as a gate for flagging these transactions, so they can be acted upon by accountants/AP team as they come in. 

Long-term, aggregated lines, that is in wider longer-term strategy process for invoice processing.

So, I will unfortunately close this ticket, as this is already relating to a problem we are aware off (linked above) and I will also link this ticket there, to highlight the Kenya impact of it. Source data from Telema is causing these issues. The rounding also causes downstream issues for tax reporting, as incorrect tax amounts are reported and manually corrected by tax team for recovering tax.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. *Key privacy considerations for AI:*

# *Assess whether you need to use AI for the context you will deploy it in.* 
## We cannot realistically remove every risk, and data protection law does not require us to do so (ICO)
# *Transparency re training and AI itself:*
## be clear, open and honest with users *from the start* about *how and why we use their personal data;*
## consider *what explanation is needed in the context* that we will deploy our AI system in;
## assess what *users are likely to expect your explanation to look like*;
## assess the *potential impact of the decisions* made by our AI system to *understand how comprehensive our explanation needs to be*; and 
## consider how we will *handle individual rights requests*: especially training: Access and retention
# *Consider which privacy-preserving techniques for the context we are using/training AI.* 
## For example, in the training phase you could use *perturbation* (adding ‘noise’), *synthetic data* or federated learning to minimise the personal data being processed. 
# *Address risks of bias and discrimination at an early stage and prepare accurate input data*
## Team would consider labelling and local communities opinion: 
### Cater to local communication nuances/context, they will be requesting Bolt internal volunteers from different countries to label messages from the countries they grew in
# *Ask the team to provide some stats before we launch the system on:*
## how an AI system guesses the correct answer, measured against correctly labelled test data. 
# *Ensure meaningful human review*
## We should ensure human reviewers are: 
##* adequately trained to interpret and challenge outputs made by the AI system; 
##* senior enough and have the authority to override an automated decision.
# *Training Scope?:*
## Fuel the model with chat data of our users
## Verify the system on real chats: _system triggers → human reviews → human checks how the system labelled the data → human makes a note in the dev documentation_
# *Legal Basis for Data Training and Transparency:*
## EDPB opinion on ChatGPT:
### The next stages concern ChatGPT input (including “prompts”), output and training. 
21. Prompts refer to the input of data subjects when interacting with LLMs such as ChatGPT as well as file uploads and the user feedback regarding the quality of the data output23 (the responses) of ChatGPT. OpenAI qualifies this as “Content” and *publicly states to use this information to train and improve the model. In this context, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR is brought forward as legal basis.24 OpenAI provides* +*the option to opt-out of the use of “Content” for training purposes. - how can we exercise this (only further processing, not past)????*+
22. Data subjects should, in any case, +*be clearly and demonstrably informed that such “Content” may be used for training purposes.*+ *This circumstance is a factor to be taken into account in the context of the balancing of interests according to Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.*
# Not transfer the responsibility for inout data to users. Take all measures to protect their data
# *DSAR:*
## Key Issues with Complying with the Right to Access:
###  *Data Identification and Segmentation:*
#### AI model is trained on vast amounts of data and would be anonymized and aggregated to the extent possible. It means that no direct identifiers would be fed in the AI model of Bolt. There is, of course, a risk that some data provided in the chat, like special categories of data, can be processed by AI model. However, the team would use privacy preserving technique to replace/mask all possible sensitive data in chats before inputting this data to AI model. 
#### Identifying specific users' data within these large datasets can be technically complex and resource-intensive. Once data is used for training, it would lose the direct identifiers, making it difficult to extract or isolate specific individuals' data. 
###  *Model Training Complexity:*
#### Training data is typically transformed into abstract representations and embedded within the model's parameters. The process involves the data being ingested, transformed, and integrated in a way that does not retain original data formats or structures. Thus, providing a "copy" of the data in its original form, as required by GDPR, becomes impractical and impossible for Bolt.
### *Bolt’s actions.* 
#### Bolt would stick to the principle of explaining which data is used for the training, what the purpose is, and provide the very chats that were used for the training.
#### !!!! Ensure/check if we mark such chats in relation to the user.
### *Security and Proprietary Concerns:*
#### Releasing the trained data or detailed internal structures of the model can pose significant security risks and expose proprietary information. It could also lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data of other users.
# Retention and Erasure:
## It’s practically impossible to erase certain user’s data upon their request because identifying specific users' data within these large datasets can be technically complex and resource-intensive. Once data is used for training, it would lose the direct identifiers, making it difficult to isolate specific individuals' data. 
## Moreover, Bolt would do the following when training the model:
###  *Implement Data Anonymization and Pseudonymization:* Transform personal data in such a way that individuals can no longer be identified. Anonymized data falls outside the scope of GDPR, mitigating storage limitation issues 
### *Implement Data Deletion and Archiving Mechanisms for row data.* Bolt would delete the row data (chats) once it is no longer needed for its original purpose. However, this aggregated and anonymised (to the extent possible) data would still be used in the trained data. Bolt cannot degrade the system due to the retention periods or individual’s requests for erasure. 
###  *User Controls:* Provide users with easy-to-use controls to opt-out of data being used for model training 
### *Data Minimization:* Bolt would collect and retain only the data that is necessary for the specific purpose of the AI model.

To proceed with the assessments and final steps, I need you to answer the following questions:

1️⃣ *Please describe how the training of the model would work*

# Do we fuel the model with *already manually labelled chat data* so that the system learns how to label or how would it look like?
# How we ensure *the data we feed in AI model is accurate* +(if we do not label the data before providing this to AI)+, so that further labelling is correct?
# *What would be in the training scope? Is the below correct?*
#* +Step 1:+ Fuel the model with manually labelled chat data of our users
#* +Step 2:+ Verify the system on real chats: _system triggers → human reviews → human checks how the system labelled the data → human makes a note in the dev documentation_

2️⃣ *Filtering some special categories of personal data and financial data*

# I appreciate this is specifically hard to filter such amounts of data or even identify patterns. However, one of the ways to reduce the risk from such a training is to anonymise data as much as possible.
## *To justify such a decision of not filtering the chat content from this data, can you please provide me with some more detailed info on:*
### why it’s a high-effort
### why it does not guarantee the this data would be masked/replaced
### approximate stats on how many chats contain such data (this would help us justify our position)
### Based on our stats of the chats, what are popular examples of such data: is this fin data, phone numbers? Do we see sharing of any documents data like No of ID, etc?
### how, from your opinion, such data being provided to the model, could potentially affect the final learning outcome of the model, if they can
## Can you please also provide the detailed explanation (so that we have it in the assessment for the data protection authorities) on *why we cannot train our model on synthetic data* (eg, this is not real user’s data, but the set of data of similar nature, but just random)?

3️⃣ *User’s right to opt-out of the training:*

# *To rely on the legal basis as legitimate interest of Bolt, we would need to introduce the option for users in the app or by contacting us to opt-out of the training of their data.*
## This is key for ensuring the lawfulness of the model training.
### Can you advise whether this would be possible to create such a button?
### *Can you advise whether it would be possible to satisfy such requests? It means when the user opts out of the training, this user chats cannot be used for further* [*training.*|http://training.It] *It does not apply to their chats we fed in before.* 

4️⃣ *Data Subject Access Right*

# As you may know, users have the right to request all data we store about them. This also applies to the data we used for the training and the final trained data (with exceptions).
## {color:#bf2600}*Can you confirm that the following would NOT be possible and I understand it right:*{color}
### *Data Identification and Segmentation:*
#### AI model is trained on vast amounts of data and would be anonymized and aggregated to the extent possible. It means that no direct identifiers would be fed in the AI model of Bolt. There is, of course, a risk that some data provided in the chat, like special categories of data, can be processed by AI model. 
#### Identifying specific users' data within these large datasets can be technically complex and resource-intensive. Once data is used for training, it would lose the direct identifiers, making it difficult to extract or isolate specific individuals' data.
### *Model Training Complexity:*
#### Training data is typically transformed into abstract representations and embedded within the model's parameters. The process involves the data being transformed and integrated in a way that does not retain original data formats or structures. Thus, providing a "copy" of the trained data, as required by GDPR, becomes impractical and impossible for Bolt.
### *Security and Proprietary Concerns:*
#### Releasing the trained data or detailed internal structures of the model can pose significant security risks and expose proprietary information. It could also lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data of other users.
## *Would we somehow label/mark in Admin which users chats were used for the training of the model?*
### This is necessary to have this, as if the user makes a request to us asking to confirm whether their chat data were used for this processing, we should know the answer and confirm this. Otherwise, we do not comply with Access request.

We do have internal _operational_ guidelines regarding when we consider speeding to be excessive.

Hey, thanks for your patience.

Regarding *the device blocking*

# We don’t need to block the devices. Using “device id” for blocking is not efficient at all because changing the device ID for the attacker is as simple as reinstalling the app. DeviceID is not a hardware identifier, it is a random value generated every time the app is (re)installed.
# On the other hand, using known deviceID as an additional security factor makes sense because unlike resetting its value, guessing its value is technically impossible. That is why we trust more if the user previously was logged in from this device. We use it as 2FA, for example instead of sending code to SMS.
# But even if the device is known and “trusted”, it is not enough to log in - there has to be a main auth factor - password, access to email, or SIM card.

During incident resolution, CS should make sure that the user password was reset, and it is only this user who has access to the given email and phone.
Otherwise, from the same device or not, the attack can be repeated. Before we launch a wider roll-out of mandatory 2fa for logins on new devices for drivers and enable password resetting in the Admin Panel, we need to rely on resetting the password manually.

I assume it’s because we still have smarthost defined as the relayhost in {{main.cf}}, and emails that fall through the relay maps are attempted to be relayed there: [https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/blob/131c1cc93692b0c7c29547771b63e64cf835cfb5/roles/ses-forwarder/files/postfix/main.cf#L23|https://github.com/bolteu/taxify-ansible/blob/131c1cc93692b0c7c29547771b63e64cf835cfb5/roles/ses-forwarder/files/postfix/main.cf#L23]

The relay maps are sender dependent so I assume the other ones are falling through because they have no FROM address specified, which would make them use the default relay host, which is {{smarthost.taxify.eu}} - a DNS name we no longer have.

For the ones sent to builder - if, after the migration, they fail to be delivered then {{root@builder.taxify.eu}} would just end up in the suppression list after it bounces for the first time, since I assume there is no mail server there. This won’t impact our bounce rate in a significant way, nor should it affect any use cases as they are failing to be sent already.

The ones with no from address shouldn’t cause any issues as they aren’t sent to customers and from the documentation it would seem that these emails just get the a default from address under {{amazonses.com}}: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/mail-from.html#mail-from-overview|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/mail-from.html#mail-from-overview]

Hi [~accountid:5f0c30effe23000022252e68], update below:

* Bolt send *may fall* under the postal services regime, insofar as the parcels qualify as postal parcels under the terms of article 5 of Law no. 17/2012, of 26 April. In this case, the provision of this activity by Bolt is subject to prior communication to ANACOM, which issues an authorisation, and the payment of fees. Hence, there is a risk that even though the law does not specifically indicates that this new service must be considered postal services, there is room for interpretation and the regulator (i.e. ANACOM) may indeed consider Bolt Send to be subject to the postal services regulation.
* After having checked the ANACOM’s website, Uber and TVDE fleets would not appear to have submitted such prior communication since they appear not to be listed in PT as postal service providers.
* Next steps:
** [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] will assess the risks in case the service is launched without prior communication under postal service legislation.
** [~accountid:5f0c30effe23000022252e68] , [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] and [~accountid:60ec731b2f97d50069db1627] to kindly confirm the decision: (i) contact ANACOM to seek their informal confirmation that no prior communication is needed or (ii) proceed with the launch even though this legal risk has been identified. 
** t&c will be finalised after this decision is taken.

Because there’s a global Business MVRA [project|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LEG-43] for Q3 strictly for globally greenlighting [“Business booking fee”|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FLRJvQtc-n706ZFnax9btP7sN0mv4jWL5NGBh0iAbhI/edit#heading=h.z45unbjfvmfw] _- a separate fee component to selected b2b trips to have more monetary maneuvering room when making certain strategic deals with Business customers (respective_ [_product functionality already exists_|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C01CFGNHQMD/p1658825325148009]_)_ - which is basically captured by yours. Are you able to share a roadmap, some deadlines, ETA’s? _Now wondering how to best progress on the Business Booking Fee project in order not to overwhelm local counsels but to ensure we progress on the priority markets (fair resource has been allocated to this in Business Q3 MVRA). Let’s chat on Mon if possible - I’ve scheduled a slot._

With regards to possible adjustments in the Business T&Cs my thinking is these are not required. Rather we would address it in Rider T&Cs because the [operational model|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1E_oOEJmYfdsduNeTPwQmQAY89fJry-fCQ7wCYpdQHbs/edit#slide=id.g14401e5ca96_0_0] (fostered by the contracting flow in the app) is such that it would still be the rider requesting the ride (but for b2b it’s just done using the Business payment method). The latter meaning any invoice would be issued to the Business customer instead anyway (per Business T&Cs). 

Principally yes, we could add any language on Business specific fees also to the Business T&Cs but the downside is, it would become immediately visible for the Business customers (and they, unlike riders, read the legal bits). And what’s visible will serve as an invite to challenge. Whereas we could instead be transparent about it in the Rider T&Cs (riders don’t care about it as Business customer has the payment obligation for primary fees anyway), and Business T&Cs make a good reference to core vertical T&Cs, and the Business customer’s obligation to pay for any User fees so. Also it would allow us to make changes to only one set of T&Cs not two (Rider + Business).

We can discuss that as well on Monday.

Cheers!

Hello [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] please find the answers below which are aligned with [~accountid:6389e5ac5fce844d606c13ed] and [~accountid:5e8437c4c8077c0c1f067163]:

{quote}# Do we fuel the model with *already manually labelled chat data* so that the system learns how to label or how would it look like?{quote}

As mentioned before, we will be creating our own internal Bolt dataset labelled by a diverse set of individuals. To train/fuel the model, only this hand-labelled data will be used.
e.g. Message: {{"You are too far away, I want 30 instead of 20"}} Intent: {{price_negotiation}} Sentiment: {{neutral}}



{quote}# How we ensure *the data we feed in AI model is accurate* (if we do not label the data before providing this to AI), so that further labelling is correct?{quote}

We can only use labelled data for an accurate model, using unlabelled data would yield a model that cannot predict anything accurately.
To ensure we have an accurate data, (1) we will be using a diverse set of human labellers, (2) a single conversation will be labelled by 2 different people so we can be sure of the high quality of the results.



{quote}What would be in the training scope? Is the below correct?
Step 1: Fuel the model with manually labelled chat data of our users
Step 2: Verify the system on real chats: system triggers → human reviews → human checks how the system labelled the data → human makes a note in the dev documentation{quote}

The human labelled data will be split into 2 parts, _training_ and _test_. The model will be trained using the _training_ data (Step 1).
Then we can verify the results using the aforementioned _test_ data and evaluate the accuracy of the model (Step 2).
Furthermore, we would test the model accuracy using the real chats as you suggested.



{quote}# I appreciate this is specifically hard to filter such amounts of data or even identify patterns. However, one of the ways to reduce the risk from such a training is to anonymise data as much as possible.

        *a. To justify such a decision of not filtering the chat content from this data, can you please provide me with some more detailed info on:*

# why it’s a high-effort
# why it does not guarantee the this data would be masked/replaced{quote}

Anonymizing large amounts of chat data requires significant manual effort and resources due to:

* High data volume: Millions of messages
* Lack of reliable & automated methods to understand context to identify what “sensitive information” is across multiple languages

As mentioned in the Slack thread, we can anonymize (i.e. replace actual numbers with random numbers) for ~99% of the {{phone numbers}} and  {{email addresses}} *automatically* as they conform to certain numerical/character patterns. Also, please note that such data (especially IBAN) are very unlikely to appear in chat data between rider and driver unless some sort of abuse is happening.



{quote}iii. approximate stats on how many chats contain such data (this would help us justify our position)
iv. Based on our stats of the chats, what are popular examples of such data: is this fin data, phone numbers? Do we see sharing of any documents data like No of ID, etc?{quote}

There is no way to answer these questions without going through millions of messages one by one. This is the main reason we want to use a machine learning model in this project.



{quote}v. how, from your opinion, such data being provided to the model, could potentially affect the final learning outcome of the model, if they can{quote}

I understand your concern about having sensitive information in the training data. As mentioned above, we will anonymize (i.e. replace actual numbers with random numbers) ~99% of the {{phone numbers}} and {{email addresses}}. 

Since the model would be trained on tens/hundreds of thousands of messages, it would learn the conceptual *associations* of e.g. sharing phone numbers _may be_ related to offline trip negotiation. So there is zero chance that model can leak any PII data.



{quote}b. Can you please also provide the detailed explanation (so that we have it in the assessment for the data protection authorities) on *why we cannot train our model on synthetic data* (eg, this is not real user’s data, but the set of data of similar nature, but just random)?{quote}

Even though using synthetic data may make sense in some context, it is *NOT* suitable for our use case due to:

# Authenticity and Realism in Data:

* Nuances of Real Data: Real user interactions capture a wide range of linguistic nuances, context-specific expressions, and variations in communication styles that are naturally present in human communication. This variation is important for training models to accurately understand and classify intents and sentiments.
* Context-Dependent Language: Real user messages often contain context-specific language that synthetic data cannot capture accurately. For example, the way users negotiate fares, provide feedback, or describe location-specific issues can vary greatly and is often influenced by cultural, regional, and situational context.
* Ambiguity: Language often contains ambiguities that require context to resolve. Real data includes naturally occurring ambiguity, allowing the model to learn how to disambiguate based on surrounding context.

# Diversity and Edge Cases:

* Edge Cases and Rare Events: Real data encompasses a variety of use cases, including rare and unusual interactions that are important for creating a robust model. Synthetic data cannot reproduce these edge cases, leading to gaps in the model’s performance.
* Natural Diversity of Expressions: Users employ different phrases, slang, idioms, and abbreviations based on their individual backgrounds and experiences. Capturing this diversity is essential for the model to generalize well to unseen data.



{quote}*User’s right to opt-out of the training:*

# *To rely on the legal basis as legitimate interest of Bolt, we would need to introduce the option for users in the app or by contacting us to opt-out of the training of their data.*
## This is key for ensuring the lawfulness of the model training.
### Can you advise whether this would be possible to create such a button?
### *Can you advise whether it would be possible to satisfy such requests? It means when the user opts out of the training, this user chats cannot be used for further training. It does not apply to their chats we fed in before.*{quote}

In Bolt [*privacy notice*|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides] *(*[Global Privacy Notice for Passengers and Riders | Bolt Legal|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides]) we have an item of {{Communication and correspondence records such as when you engage with our in-app chat, or speak with our customer service agents.}} under {{1. Personal data we process}} . 

It is also noted under {{2. Purpose of Processing}} that {{Instant messages directly in the Bolt app are processed in order to provide service and customer support (including resolving disputes between driver and rider), for security purposes as well as to improve our products and services, and for analysis.}}
There is no difference from this processing to training machine learning models. The privacy notice already covers the collected data of in-app chat and purpose of security and improving the service.
*To my understanding, we do not require any additional permits from users since it is already covered*. Please correct me if I am wrong here.

Regarding satisfying opt-out requests, *Yes*, of course, if they have opted-out, we can exclude any chat data from any user in the dataset.

It is important to highlight the fact that chat data is a crucial element in providing security to our platform: Otherwise fraudsters can just opt-out and our platform would become more dangerous.


❗ Finally, I would like to mention this important point explicitly: 

*The in-house machine learning model in question that we plan to train is* *_NOT_* *an “AI model” as in OpenAI’s ChatGPT*. 

👉 It *won’t* have any text generation or chatting capabilities. 

👉 It can only output: The *intent of chat message from one of the 6 categories* (aggressive harassment, sexual harassment, offline trip negotiation, price negotiation, phishing, impersonation).

👉 There is *zero chance of getting/leaking PII data* from the model.

It is simply a machine learning model like any other hundreds of models developed and used in Bolt.

[~accountid:712020:8fd75aa8-dcfb-42ad-93ab-53900ee4c301] looping you in here for some German civil law insight. Can you let me know if there are any holes in my assessment (below)?

The case at hand can be summarized as follows: A Bolt Drive user ended their ride with Bolt’s car and parked the car so that it blocked the entrance/exit of a business (our claimant). The car was parked within Bolt Operating Area (meaning, the App allowed the car to be parked there), but _presumably_ in breach of traffic laws (as it was blocking an exit to a business) and therefore also in breach of Bolt T&Cs (as we oblige our users to follow all traffic laws, including when parking the vehicle). Since Bolt is the owner of the vehicle, the claimant contacted our Customer Support in order to get the vehicle removed. As the claimant received no response from our CS, they towed the vehicle. Now they are claiming for damages caused by lost work hours (the time when the vehicle was blocking their exit).

I checked the Road Traffic Act and my initial assessment is that their claim is unfounded. The vehicle holder (Fahrzeughalter) is only liable if during the operation of the vehicle, a person suffers death, the body or health of a person is injured or an item of property is damaged (Section 7(1) of the Road Traffic Act). None of these circumstances apply here. Since the user parked the car, this claim should be directed at them.

Let me know if you agree. The only counterargument to this I can think of is that since the user ended their ride (i.e., they were no longer operating the vehicle and therefore not responsible for relocating it), then it is Bolt’s responsibility to eventually relocate the vehicle if it was parked in an illegal way, and Bolt essentially failed this when the claimant received no response form our CS.

     all_offers_count AS (select count(*) as all_cnt
                          from all_offers),
     all_going_offline AS (select *
                           from glue.ng_public.company_driver_state_log dsl
                           where dsl.created_date = cast('2024-08-08' as date)
                             AND dsl.driver_city_id in
                                 (select id from glue.ng_public.admin_system_city where name = 'Bangkok')
                             AND state = 'inactive'
                             AND update_reason NOT IN ('driver_rejected', 'driver_did_not_respond'))
select off.id IS NOT NULL as going_offline_within_3_sec_of_offer_create,
       off.update_reason,
       count(*)           AS cnt
from all_offers ao
         LEFT join all_going_offline off
                   ON abs(date_diff('second', ao.created, off.created)) < 3 AND off.driver_id = ao.driver_id AND
                      off.driver_city_id = ao.city_id
where ao.state = 'rejected'
  AND ao.reject_reason = 'driver_did_not_respond'
group by 1, 2
ORDER BY cnt desc
;{noformat}

Hi Farooq,

We have a monthly options awarding process in place - at the beginning of each month, we grant options that were requested during the previous month or which have grant date marked to be in the previous month.

Although your promotion was effective as of 1.05.2024, the request for promised stock options was made only in July, meaning that we could process this only at the beginning of August.

Options cannot be awarded in the past due to legal, reporting and financial reasons, which means that the only way to keep the promise to you regarding vesting details was to use custom vesting schedule for your grant, making sure that even though units were awarded to you 2 months late, they vest as if were awarded to you in May. 
I.e., if the grant date would have been 1.05.2024 then you would have vested your first portion of units in 3 months, so on 30.07.2024, second portion another 3 months later, so 30.10.2024, and so on until your grant would have become fully vested on 30.04.2028.
Now as the grant date was 2 months later, but custom vesting schedule is in place, then your initial earn out happened on 2.07.2024, second one will happen on 30.10.2024, and so on until your grant becomes fully vested on 30.04.2028 (4 years minus 1 day from grant date).

You can see the vesting schedule attached to your grant in Carta.

Let me know if any questions remain.

Kind regards

Hi [~accountid:6411c587f1b529dfa98c0e66], 

The Canadian entity is a provincial entity incorporated in the province of Ontario. However, since Bolt will be conducting business in Quebec as well we needed to make an extra-provincial registration in Quebec. Hence, there are two (2) different registration numbers: 

* Ontario registration number (main incorporation number) 
* Quebec registration number (extra-provincial registration) 

The Ontario number is the main entity number and this is also where Bolt has its reporting obligations (incl. financial statements). 

The Quebec registration number is required for Quebec specific business activities. 

Please note that the reporting obligation in Quebec is related to the information disclosed on the REQ database (financial statements are not included). A Québec registrant must file an updating declaration stating that the information contained in the register is accurate or, as applicable, stating what changes should be made. This obligation begins the year following the year in which the Québec registrant is first registered.

The vehicle holder (Fahrzeughalter) can only be liable if the vehicle operator cannot be identified or it would be unreasonable to do so (section 25a StVG) or if during the operation of the vehicle, a person suffers death, the body or health of a person is injured or an item of property is damaged (section 7 StVG). Furthermore, their claim for loss of revenue is unproven and the burden of proof lies with them.

Hi Enelys! After a technical investigation, into options, the following assessment has been complete:

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
When supplier is being created, it is a global object. We do not currently limit suppliers to only be used to Entity X or Entity Y. This means that when the bank account is being added, it is also being added under the *Country* field, and not legal entity.
{panel}

We have few options from technical standpoint: 

* *Option 1: Bank Account Configuration -* we have an option to make the BIC required, optional or do not show. However, we do this as *country* level meaning *all* bank accounts in Estonia would require to have the bank identification code. This includes suppliers, customers and employees. So this means that all employees based in Estonia would need to also update their bank information to have BIC included. This may be the right option, but it brings a lot of change management. 

!image-20240812-113605.png|width=1450,height=565,alt="image-20240812-113605.png"!



* *Option 2: Restricted to Companies & Validation -* there is a field called restricted to companies, which before we’ve talked about in supplier request/onboarding process. If you were to select the companies that this supplier will be using i.e. Bolt Technology OU, or Bolt Operations OU (can be multiple) then this would enable myself to build the custom validation, ensuring that : 

IF Restricted to Companies = Bolt Technology OR Bolt Operations THEN BIC must be filled

!image-20240812-113746.png|width=990,height=362,alt="image-20240812-113746.png"!



* *Option 3: Invoice Validation  -* We can build a validation, at the point of *invoice creation* where an invoice is submitted, and we will look up the supplier, to determine whether they have a BIC code or not. When an invoice is submitted from Telema, into Workday, we can then auto-trigger the validation and state “This supplier requires a BIC code!” and that will be able to be managed through supplier invoice work area. Then when BIC is added, you would be able to re-submit the invoice fine. Alternatively, we can look at putting this validation on the supplier settlement meaning that we’d flag any invoices where a BIC code is not input prior to paying those invoices. 



* *Option 4: Validation Report -* the last option that I can think off, is to build you a report once invoices are received, to show you which suppliers do and which do not have a bank identification code filled out for Bolt Operations & Bolt Technology invoices, but this would be more on historical data and would not give you that assurance that when new invoices come in, then they’d be paid out fine.

Please let me know your preference on the options, and how to proceed further! 🙂 

Witek

Hello,

We have discussed this issue with SOM and would like to ask several questions, as well as provide some details about the current situation in Lithuania regarding the compliance of addresses.

*Context:*

In Lithuania, all drivers are self-employed and act as independent entities. They are not employed by, nor do they have any work relations with, Nolt or any other companies.

When submitting their application for a self-employment ID (individual activity certificate), individuals are not required to provide a specific address. They can enter their home address (declared place of residency) or any other address. *During submission, they only need to tick a box confirming whether the address provided is their declared home address.*

Additionally, Lithuania does not have a publicly available address database for individuals, only for companies. *This means we cannot verify the validity of a private person’s address.*

*This situation presents several challenges:*

* We cannot verify the address through a public database.
* If we request proof of address from drivers, we cannot ensure it is where they actually reside, nor can we track any changes to that address.
* Drivers are under no obligation to inform us if their address changes.
* As a result, we cannot guarantee that the addresses will be accurate on the day of the DAC7 report.

From an operational perspective, and considering the process of obtaining an individual activity certificate, this appears to be a compliance gap in our country and seems more like a bureaucracy issue to us. 

Recent events related to VMI (Lithuania's tax authority) not accepting DAC7 reports in a convenient format have highlighted this issue. We would like to ask if there are any alternatives available that would allow us to ensure compliance without adding additional documentation burdens. 

*Please keep in mind that we cannot verify the validity of any private address, there is no technical means for drivers to update their address in our system, and registering for individual activity does not require the individual to enter a valid address.*

Based on our experience with VMI requests, we have never encountered issues with addresses, leading us to believe that VMI does not track or verify them when processing tax data.

*Some alternatives we thought about:*

- Maybe writing one address under all profiles (for example, municipality, or Bolt Services) could overcome this issue.

{code:sql}SELECT 
date(date_trunc('week',x.created_date)) AS week,
--x.country,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.orderlink,0.0041) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(AVG(x.driven_distance) AS double),0) AS avg_driven_distance,
ROUND(CAST(AVG(x.min_predicted_distance) AS double),0) AS avg_min_predicted_distance,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.lost_commission_eur) AS double),2) AS sum_lost_commission_eur
FROM (
WITH destinations_distances AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
a.meta.order_id,
a.meta.city_id,
(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.features.distances.arrived_to_driving') AS REAL) + CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.features.distances.driving_to_destination') AS REAL)) AS driven_distance, -- there's room TO improve here. doesn't cover scenario WHERE driver doesn't arrive AT the pickup. can SUM accepted_to_arrived, but need to take distance from acceptance to pickup into consideration then. instead of only predicted distance. 
ROUND(great_circle_distance(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.locations.destination.lat') AS REAL),CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.locations.destination.lng') AS REAL),cod.destination_lat,cod.destination_lng),2) AS distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest
FROM archive_analytical.ridehailing_driver_order_completed_check a
JOIN ng_public.company_order_destination cod ON a.meta.order_id = cod.order_id AND a.meta.city_id = cod.city_id 
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-07-01'
AND cod.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
),
min_distance AS (
SELECT  
cod.order_id AS order_id,
cod.city_id AS city_id,
d.driven_distance,
MIN(CASE WHEN d.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN d.distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest END) AS min_distance_to_dest_km
FROM ng_public.company_order_destination cod
JOIN destinations_distances d ON cod.order_id = d.order_id AND cod.city_id = d.city_id
WHERE cod.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
),
prediction_data AS (
SELECT  
a.order_id,
a.city_id,
MAX(a.predicted_price)/r.rate AS predicted_price_eur, -- USING max here TO calculate max impact
MIN(a.distance) AS min_predicted_distance -- IN CASE OF multiple predictions, USING MIN assures that AT least part OF the ORDER happened
FROM ng_public.pricing_order_prediction a 
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON a.order_id = ot.order_id AND a.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected' AND ot.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
JOIN ng_public.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(ot.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
GROUP BY 1,2,r.rate
)
SELECT DISTINCT 
ot.created_date,
ot.order_id,
ot.city_id,
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/' || CAST(ot.order_id AS varchar) || '/' || CAST(ot.city_id AS varchar) AS orderlink,
co.country,
md.driven_distance,
ROUND(CAST(p.min_predicted_distance AS double),0) AS min_predicted_distance,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(md.driven_distance*1.00/NULLIF(p.min_predicted_distance,0) AS double),2),0) AS driven_distance_ratio,
md.min_distance_to_dest_km,
p.predicted_price_eur,
p.predicted_price_eur*0.25 AS lost_commission_eur
FROM ng_public.etl_fact_company_order_try_state_log_transposed ot
JOIN prediction_data p ON ot.order_id = p.order_id AND ot.city_id = p.city_id
JOIN min_distance md ON ot.order_id = md.order_id AND ot.city_id = md.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public.company_order co ON ot.order_id = co.id AND ot.city_id = co.city_id AND co.created_date >= date '2024-07-01'
WHERE ot.created_date_local >= date '2024-07-01'
AND ot.state = 'driver_rejected'
AND (md.min_distance_to_dest_km <= 0.5 OR (md.min_distance_to_dest_km <= 1 AND md.driven_distance >= 3000))
AND COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(md.driven_distance*1.00/NULLIF(p.min_predicted_distance,0) AS double),2),0) >= 0.5
AND md.driven_distance >= 500
) AS x
GROUP BY 1--,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

{noformat}for i in $(seq 1800000 50000 5850000); do

Hello [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] :

*Summary:*

The advice looks correct and we will indeed need *opt-in* from users in Dubai to send direct marketing.

A record of consent is especially important for SMS - Bolt will be required to upload a consent database on the Consent Management Service (CMS) platform for approval from the local operator (afaik, in our case - [Etisalat|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-36293?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMzU2ZGY2YWE1MjU2NDQ2MWJmMjRiNjI4YjZiNWZhNmYiLCJwIjoiamlyYS1zbGFjay1pbnQifQ]) to prevent their SMS messages from being blocked.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Applicable law:*

* Regulations on Unsolicited Electronic Communication (RUEC)
*  Mobile Marketing SMS Regulatory Policy
* DIFC Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020 (applicable in DIFC only)
* Federal Law No. 45 of 2021 (applies extra-territorially) 
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Scope:*

All electronic communications conveyed by means of a telecommunications network to an electronic address, which in the context of Bolt should include:

* SMS (rules outlined by Etisalat [here|https://www.etisalat.ae/en/system/wst/assets/docs/business/general/etisalat-consent-management-service-policy.pdf])
* Email
* WhatsApp messages and similar services
* Push notifications

*Seems the rules apply both to B2C and B2B context, where the recipient is an individual.* If the recipient is a legal person (i.e., fleets, drivers) - seems rules do not apply. No clear guidelines on the topic.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Enforcement:*

According to [Data Guidance|https://www.dataguidance.com/opinion/uae-overview-direct-marketing-requirements]:

Fine of not less than AED 5,000 (approx. $1,360) and not more than AED 200,000 (approx. $54,450). Where the application of the RUEC is indirect (compliance is required as an obligation under the licensed service provider's terms and conditions), then non-compliance would be a breach of contract. However, the real enforcement mechanism is blocking the messaging. 

Probability - not clear.
{panel}

Thanks [~accountid:63cfbe91c565900ff404f491] and apologies for the delay. The email, form and competition itself raise a few data protection considerations that I needed to think about - I set out our analysis on each consideration below.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#403294}*IN SUMMARY:*{color}

* Emailing the form to the drivers to promote the competition does not raise any blockers, provided we are not also calling the drivers (see *point (1)* below for further info)
* Please {color:#4c9aff}*provide me with a copy of the agreement*{color} governing this campaign (e.g., is it the [Campaign T&C|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ybRlet8ae-IPsv5T7MemwjSEYiNGi0afYS5DQS3Nzb8/edit]?). To the extent not already implemented, the {color:#4c9aff}*wording of this agreement should be updated*{color} to ensure that it explicitly covers what personal data of the driver will be processed, and why (see *points (2) and (3)* below for context).
* Some {color:#4c9aff}*additional wording should be included in the form*{color} which hyperlinks to the agreement governing this campaign. I have drafted some wording that can be used below (see *point (2)* below).
* Collecting: (a) the number of completed trips; (b) the average rating; and (c) the number of driver codes used by friends to determine winners of the competition should be fine, provided that these activities are clearly included in the relevant agreement and the criteria are explicitly defined (see *point (3)* below).
* {color:#ff5630}*We do not advise collecting information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS*{color} to determine a winner (see *point (3)* below).
* [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] - Does this competition present any obvious issues with regards to being seen as 'Bolt encouraging drivers to drive more’?
{panel}

----

*(1) Sending the email / form to the drivers*

As hinted at below, it would be {color:#4c9aff}*better to just email the drivers*{color} rather than also call them. This is because in conducting this competition we should not be processing any personal information that is unnecessary, and phone numbers could be regarded as unnecessary where email is an option.

Our legal basis for sending these emails would be +legitimate interest+ (i.e., Bolt’s legitimate interest in promoting our services and conducting sweepstakes to deepen our existing relationship with our drivers / develop new ones). 

Please note that Bolt’s processing of driver personal data in this context is not currently covered in the live Driver Privacy Notice. This is a known risk, and is being covered in the updated version of the Driver Privacy Notice that is due to be rolled out by the end of August. In the meantime, there is already some disclaimer wording on Bolt’s [website|https://bolt.eu/en/driver/] to address transparency requirements, and so the overall risk here is low / this does not act as a blocker.

----

*(2) Collecting the driver’s email and name through the form*

Collecting this information is low risk, and our legal basis for doing so is likely to be +contractual necessity+ (i.e., collecting this information is necessary to perform the competition T&C between Bolt and the driver). However, before I can confirm this legal basis - could you please {color:#4c9aff}*confirm / provide me with a copy of the agreement / T&C that govern this competition*{color}? Is it the [Campaign T&C|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ybRlet8ae-IPsv5T7MemwjSEYiNGi0afYS5DQS3Nzb8/edit]? We need to make sure that collecting the driver’s name and email for the purpose of determining and announcing the winner is mentioned in the agreement (see for example Section 6.2 in the [Campaign T&C|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ybRlet8ae-IPsv5T7MemwjSEYiNGi0afYS5DQS3Nzb8/edit]).

If this is the case, then {color:#4c9aff}*we should add wording to the form which states the following*{color}:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
“_We conduct this competition based on the [Campaign T&C]. For more information on how Bolt processes your personal data in the context of this competition, please refer to [Section 6 of the Campaign T&C]: [LINK]._”
{panel}

This is important from a transparency perspective, given that (as above) this processing activity is not explicitly covered in the live Driver Privacy Notice, and so we should include some transparency wording to cover our bases until we can update the Driver Privacy Notice by the end of August.

----

*(3) Processing the driver’s data to check whether any of the three conditions are met*

+Condition 1 - Most completed trips+

I understand that to measure this metric, we intend to process: (1) the number of rides completed by the driver; and (2) information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS.

Collecting the total number of a driver’s completed trips in this context makes sense and is for a clear purpose, and so we have no concerns here from a privacy perspective. The legal basis here would be the same as above (i.e., +contractual necessity+) - as such, we need to make sure that collecting this information for the purpose of determining and announcing the winner is {color:#4c9aff}*mentioned in the agreement*{color}, for the sake of transparency. It should be concise and clearly defined.

{color:#ff5630}*We do not advise collecting and reviewing information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS in the context of this competition*{color}, if this can be avoided. This is because:

* This information is quite high risk. It seems intrusive, and drivers are unlikely to expect that this kind of information would be collected in the context of a competition.
* There is a potential issue here in terms of fairness. You mention that eligible drivers are those whose profiles are “_“clean”, without or with just a few low / moderate number of past issues_”, as well as those who are not “_rude_” to CS - however, it is not  clear to me how we would decide on these issues. The criteria for choosing the winners of this competition must be clear to ensure fairness, and it may be difficult to set out these criteria to the user definitively (unless you have already prepared something on this - in which case let me know).

As such, if it is possible to just measure the number of completed rides without undermining the competition, we would recommend doing so.

+Condition 2 - Rider ratings+

I understand that to measure this metric, we intend to process: (1) the driver’s average rating; and (2) information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS.

My conclusions on this are the same as for Condition 1. In short:

* Collecting the driver’s rating should be fine. However, this should be {color:#4c9aff}*mentioned in the agreement*{color}. It should be concise and clearly defined.
* {color:#ff5630}*We do not advise collecting and reviewing information on any safety / quality cases and interactions with CS in the context of this competition*{color}, for the reasons set out above.

+Condition 3 - Most friends invited+

I understand that to measure this metric, we only intend to process the number of ‘codes’ of the driver that have been used. This make sense and is for a clear purpose, and so we have no concerns here from a privacy perspective. The legal basis here would be the same as above (i.e., +contractual necessity+) - as such, we need to make sure that collecting this information for the purpose of determining and announcing the winner is {color:#4c9aff}*mentioned in the agreement*{color}, for the sake of transparency. It should be concise and clearly defined.

Finally, [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] - {color:#6554c0}*Does this competition present any obvious issues with regards to being seen as 'Bolt encouraging drivers to drive more’*{color}? We are dealing with reclassification risk in the UK so wanted to check whether there are any similar issues from a Lithuanian perspective.

h1. Idea

The idea is to have the same user interaction controls in Slack as we have in Builder UI.

h1. Cases

Let’s review 2 general cases.

h2. Regular buttons such as “Continue” & “Abort”, etc in the pipeline steps

!image-20240813-073848.png|width=519,height=134,alt="image-20240813-073848.png"!

For each step that is waiting for user interaction and can be handled by [handleUserInteraction|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/1b74712d6083df176345af9454c67178f7c521a5/builder/packages/backend/src/builder/service/BuilderService.ts#L594] Builder sends a message to the pipeline owner via Slack bot with the same [buttons|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/1b74712d6083df176345af9454c67178f7c521a5/builder/packages/backend/src/builder/service/BuildActionStep.ts#L135] as we have in step.ui.

h2. Deployment step

!image-20240813-074114.png|width=1124,height=158,alt="image-20240813-074114.png"!

Send a message with one button for each environment: “DEPLOY ALL”. This will cover the majority of cases.

Later, we can consider sending additional messages for each package in every environment to provide the same flexibility as Builder has. However, in some cases with multiple packages (>5), there will be too many messages from Slack bot

h1. Solution

However, *we only use Slack API to send messages* using [postMessage|https://github.com/bolteu/backend-platform/blob/1b74712d6083df176345af9454c67178f7c521a5/builder/packages/backend/src/builder/service/NotificationService.ts#L616].

Technically, there are two options to achieve that:

# Using [https://api.slack.com/interactivity/handling|https://api.slack.com/interactivity/handling] 
# Using [https://api.slack.com/apis/events-api|https://api.slack.com/apis/events-api]

Both *require having a publicly available HTTP endpoint*.

h1. Implementation

There are many options for implementing the external endpoint.

# Create and expose one endpoint with an external router from the Builder package directly, which eventually will call handleUserInteraction.
# Create a universal proxy for multipurpose in unotice service
## (optional) Switch to unotice in Builder

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 12 August.

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Trip history*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt
